lessons.title: Designing Sheep Barns
lessons.body: A good sheep barn keeps animals dry, well-ventilated, and easy to manage. In Africa, you can build a simple, low-cost barn using local materials like wooden poles, mud bricks, or burnt bricks. Aim for 1.5 to 2 square metres per adult sheep. For a flock of 20 ewes, that's a barn about 4 metres by 8 metres. The floor should be raised 30â50 cm above ground with slats or packed earth to prevent dampness. If using concrete, slope it 1:20 for drainage. Walls can be open on one side with wire mesh for airflow; solid walls on the windward side if it's cold. The roof should be corrugated iron or thatch, with a ridge vent to let hot air escape. Aisles: at least 1.2 m wide for feeding and cleaning. Build a feed trough along one wall, 40 cm deep, with a neck rail to stop sheep walking in feed. Include a small pen for sick animals and a lambing pen (1.5 m x 1.5 m per ewe). Place the barn on high ground, away from swamps, and orient it east-west to reduce sun heating. For 50 sheep, you need about 100 square metres. Use treated poles for posts to resist termites. Remember: sheep hate mud and draughts. A dry, airy barn reduces pneumonia and foot rot. You can add a simple office and feed store at one end, separated by a wall. Cost: roughly $500â$1500 for a 50-sheep barn using local labour and materials. Always allow space for a future expansion. Ventilation is key: ammonia from urine can cause lung damage. If you smell ammonia, increase openings. In hot climates, consider a shade barn with only a roof and no walls. In cold highlands, use closed walls with small vents. Build strong doors that open outward. Finally, make sure the barn is predator-proof: no gaps larger than 10 cm at the bottom, and wire mesh on windows.

lessons.title: Fencing and Handling Systems
lessons.body: Fencing keeps your sheep in, predators out, and allows rotational grazing. For permanent boundary fences, use wooden posts every 3â4 metres, with 5â6 strands of galvanised wire. The bottom wire should be 15 cm from ground, then every 15â20 cm. For sheep, woven wire with 15 cm squares is best; barbed wire can tear fleece. In Africa, live fences like sisal, thorny acacia, or euphorbia work well and are cheap. Plant them 1 m apart; they take 2â3 years to form a barrier. For internal paddocks, electric fencing is effective: one or two strands of polywire at 30 cm and 60 cm heights, powered by a 12V battery or solar energiser. Sheep respect electric fences after one shock. Handling systems reduce stress. Build a race (chute) 60 cm wide and 1.2 m high, with solid sides. At the end, a forcing pen with a curved race leading to a squeeze chute or a tipping table for shearing. Use a drafting gate to sort sheep. For foot trimming, a simple tilt table made from a wooden platform and a rope works. A lambing jug (1.5 m x 1.5 m) is essential for bonding. All handling areas should be on a concrete or gravel pad to prevent mud. When moving sheep, use a dog or a bucket of feed; never chase. Install a loading ramp 1 m high for trucks. For shearing, a clean, shaded area with a wooden floor. In hot climates, provide shade over the race. Fencing materials cost: $200â$500 per 100 m for wire and posts. Electric fence kit: $150â$300. Always check fences weekly for breaks and shorts. Predator control: add an apron of wire mesh on the ground outside the fence, 60 cm wide, to stop digging. For jackals and foxes, electric strands at 20 cm and 40 cm help. Keep grass short near fences. Handling systems should be designed so one person can move 50 sheep in an hour. Use a dog if trained; otherwise, train sheep to come to a call. Finally, ensure all gates are 1 m wide and swing freely.

lessons.title: Shelter for Different Climates
lessons.body: Africa has diverse climates: hot deserts, humid tropics, cool highlands, and semi-arid savannas. Your shelter must match. In hot, dry areas (e.g., Sahel), use a simple shade structure: four poles and a corrugated iron or thatch roof, open on all sides. Provide 2â3 square metres per sheep. The roof should be 2.5â3 m high to allow heat to rise. White-painted roofs reflect heat. In humid tropics (e.g., West Africa), you need raised floors and good ventilation to prevent foot rot and pneumonia. Build a barn with open sides and a raised slatted floor 1 m above ground. Use bamboo or treated timber slats 5 cm wide with 2 cm gaps. In cool highlands (e.g., Ethiopia, Kenya), sheep need protection from cold winds and rain. Use a closed barn with a solid wall on the windward side, and open the leeward side. Provide deep bedding (straw or wood shavings) 15 cm thick. In semi-arid areas, a three-sided shed facing away from prevailing winds works. For all climates, ensure drainage: dig a 30 cm deep trench around the barn. In hot climates, add a wallowing area? No, sheep don't wallow. Instead, provide shade trees. In cold climates, avoid draughts but allow fresh air. Use a thermometer: keep barn between 10Â°C and 25Â°C. In deserts, nights can be cold; a closed shelter with vents helps. In all cases, orientation: long axis east-west to minimise sun exposure. Roof overhang 50 cm to keep rain out. In humid zones, use treated timber to resist termites. For a 30-sheep flock, a 6 m x 10 m shelter costs $300â$800. You can also use existing buildings, but ensure they have good airflow. In flood-prone areas, build on a 50 cm high platform. Always provide a dry lying area. In hot climates, sprinkle water on the roof? That wastes water. Instead, use reflective roof. In cold climates, use curtains that can be rolled down at night. Finally, observe your sheep: if they pant, it's too hot; if they huddle, it's too cold.

lessons.title: Bedding and Waste Management
lessons.body: Bedding keeps sheep clean, dry, and warm, and absorbs urine. Use straw, wood shavings, rice hulls, or dried leaves. In Africa, maize stover, groundnut haulms, or chopped sorghum stalks work well. Apply 10â15 cm of bedding in pens. For a 20-sheep pen, you need about 2 bales of straw per week. Deep bedding systems (where you add fresh bedding on top without removing) can work for 3â6 months, but you must keep it dry. The bedding should be changed when it becomes wet or smells of ammonia. For a small flock, clean pens weekly; for larger, use a deep litter system and clean twice a year. Waste management: sheep manure is valuable fertiliser. Collect manure and urine-soaked bedding and compost it. Build a compost heap 1.5 m high, 2 m wide, and 2 m long. Turn it every 2 weeks. In 6â8 weeks, it becomes black, crumbly compost. Apply to crops at 2â4 tonnes per hectare. Do not let manure runoff into water sources; keep compost 30 m from wells. For urine, use a concrete floor with a drain to a covered pit. The liquid can be diluted 1:10 with water and used as foliar feed. In hot climates, flies are a problem. Sprinkle lime or wood ash on fresh manure to reduce odours and flies. You can also use fly traps. For bedding, avoid sawdust from treated wood (toxic). If using sand bedding, it must be cleaned daily. In humid areas, bedding can grow mould; keep it dry by ventilating. For lambing pens, use fresh, clean bedding. After lambing, remove soiled bedding. Manure can be sold to crop farmers: a 50 kg bag sells for $2â$5. A 50-sheep flock produces about 1 tonne of manure per month. Use a wheelbarrow and shovel for small flocks; for large, a tractor with a scraper. Always wear gloves and boots when handling manure. Composted manure improves soil health and reduces the need for chemical fertiliser. Finally, store bedding under cover to keep it dry.

lessons.title: Water Supply Systems
lessons.body: Sheep need 4â8 litres of clean water per day, more in hot weather (up to 12 litres). A lactating ewe can drink 10 litres. Water must be fresh, cool, and free of contamination. For a flock of 50, you need at least 300 litres per day. Options: borehole, well, river, or rainwater harvesting. A hand pump or solar pump is ideal. Store water in a tank (1000â5000 litres) on a 2 m high stand for gravity flow. Piping: use 20 mm PVC pipes to troughs. Troughs should be 40 cm deep, with a float valve to maintain level. For small flocks, use 20-litre buckets secured to a fence; but they tip over. Better: a concrete trough 1 m long, 30 cm wide, 25 cm deep, with a drain plug. Place troughs in shade to keep water cool. Clean troughs daily: scrub with a brush and rinse. Add 1 ml of bleach per 10 litres of water if algae grows. In hot climates, provide water twice daily; in cold, once. Always have water available. For winter, prevent freezing by using black pipes or a heated bowl. For remote areas, use a solar-powered pump with a 12V battery. Cost: a solar pump kit $200â$500. Rainwater: roof catchment of 10 mÂ² yields 10 litres per mm of rain. A 2000-litre tank costs $150â$300. For a 50-sheep farm, a 5000-litre tank is safe. Test water quality: it should have less than 1000 ppm total dissolved solids. If using river water, filter through sand and cloth. Avoid stagnant water; it causes liver flukes. For automatic waterers, use a nose pump that sheep learn to press. But simpler: a trough with a float valve connected to a tank. In cold highlands, insulate pipes. In all cases, keep troughs at a height of 30â40 cm so sheep can drink comfortably. Provide one trough per 25 sheep to reduce competition. Check water daily. Dehydration causes death in 24 hours. Finally, train sheep to use new waterers by leading them with a familiar bucket.

lessons.title: Predator Control Structures
lessons.body: Predators like jackals, foxes, wild dogs, leopards, and eagles can kill lambs and weak sheep. In Africa, the most common are jackals and domestic dogs. Strong fencing is your first defence. Use woven wire 1.2 m high, buried 30 cm into the ground, and add a 60 cm wire apron on the outside, pegged down. For climbing predators, add a wire overhang at the top, angled outward. Electric fencing: run 3 strands at 20 cm, 40 cm, and 60 cm heights, powered by a 12V energiser. This shocks predators and trains them to stay away. For night protection, bring sheep into a predator-proof kraal: walls 1.5 m high, made of stone, mud brick, or wire mesh with a roof. The kraal should have a solid gate that closes tightly. For leopards, a roof is essential. For eagles, use overhead netting or keep lambs indoors. Guardian animals: donkeys, llamas, or specially trained dogs (Anatolian Shepherd, Kangal) work well. A donkey will chase jackals. A dog needs training and feeding. In Africa, use local dogs that are bonded with sheep from puppyhood. Lighting: a solar-powered motion light scares predators. Noise: radios or bells. But the best is a secure kraal at night. For lambs, keep them in a small pen near the house. For a 50-sheep flock, a kraal of 10 m x 10 m with 1.5 m walls costs $200â$500. Use thorny branches (acacia) woven into the fence as an extra barrier. Check fences daily for holes. Remove tall grass and bushes near fences where predators hide. In areas with lions, you need a fully roofed enclosure. For jackals, an electric fence is very effective. Always count your sheep at night. If you lose an animal, set a trap or call wildlife authorities. Never use poison; it kills non-target animals. Finally, keep a record of losses to identify patterns. A well-built kraal reduces predation by 90%.

quiz.q: What is the recommended floor space per adult sheep in a barn?
quiz.explanation: 1.5â2 square metres per adult sheep allows for movement and reduces stress.

quiz.q: Why should a sheep barn floor be raised 30â50 cm above ground?
options: A) To make it easier to clean
B) To prevent dampness and disease
quiz.explanation: A raised floor prevents dampness, which causes foot rot and pneumonia.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a ridge vent in a sheep barn roof?
options: B) To allow hot air to escape
quiz.explanation: Hot air rises and escapes through the ridge vent, keeping the barn cool.

quiz.q: Which material is best for a permanent boundary fence for sheep?
options: B) Woven wire with 15 cm squares
quiz.explanation: Woven wire with 15 cm squares prevents sheep from getting their heads stuck and keeps predators out.

quiz.q: What is the ideal height for electric fence strands for sheep?
quiz.explanation: Sheep respect electric fences when strands are at 30 cm and 60 cm, which are nose and shoulder height.

quiz.q: What is a forcing pen used for in a handling system?
options: B) To move sheep into a race
quiz.explanation: A forcing pen funnels sheep into a race or chute for handling.

quiz.q: In hot, dry climates, what type of shelter is recommended?
options: B) Shade structure open on all sides
quiz.explanation: A shade structure with open sides allows maximum airflow and prevents overheating.

quiz.q: Why is a raised slatted floor important in humid tropics?
options: B) To prevent foot rot and pneumonia
quiz.explanation: A raised slatted floor keeps sheep off wet ground, reducing foot rot and respiratory diseases.

quiz.q: What is the recommended thickness of bedding in a sheep pen?
quiz.explanation: 10â15 cm of bedding absorbs urine and provides comfort.

quiz.q: How often should you turn a compost heap of sheep manure?
quiz.explanation: Turning every 2 weeks speeds up decomposition and kills pathogens.

quiz.q: What is a safe distance to keep a compost heap from a well?
quiz.explanation: 30 metres prevents runoff from contaminating drinking water.

quiz.q: How much water does a lactating ewe need per day?
quiz.explanation: A lactating ewe can drink up to 10 litres per day to produce milk.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a float valve in a water trough?
options: B) To maintain a constant water level
quiz.explanation: A float valve automatically refills the trough as sheep drink.

quiz.q: How many litres of water can a 10 mÂ² roof catchment collect per mm of rain?
quiz.explanation: 1 mm of rain on 1 mÂ² yields 1 litre, so 10 mÂ² yields 10 litres.

quiz.q: What is the best way to prevent water from freezing in winter?
options: B) Use black pipes or heated bowls
quiz.explanation: Black pipes absorb heat, and heated bowls keep water liquid.

quiz.q: What is the most effective predator control structure for night protection?
options: B) A predator-proof kraal with roof
quiz.explanation: A fully enclosed kraal with a roof prevents climbing and digging predators.

quiz.q: Which animal is commonly used as a guardian for sheep in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Donkeys are aggressive towards jackals and other predators.

quiz.q: Why should you bury the bottom of a woven wire fence 30 cm into the ground?
options: B) To prevent predators from digging under
D) To allow grass to grow
quiz.explanation: Burying the wire stops digging predators like jackals.

quiz.q: What is the recommended height for a predator-proof kraal wall?
quiz.explanation: 1.5 m is high enough to deter most predators from jumping over.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a lambing jug?
options: B) To isolate a ewe and her lambs for bonding
quiz.explanation: A lambing jug allows the ewe and lambs to bond without interference.

quiz.q: What is the ideal width of a sheep race (chute)?
quiz.explanation: 60 cm is wide enough for sheep to move but narrow enough to prevent turning around.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign that a sheep barn is too hot?
options: B) Sheep pant and seek shade
quiz.explanation: Panting and seeking shade indicate heat stress.

quiz.q: What is the best bedding material to avoid?
options: B) Wood shavings from treated wood
quiz.explanation: Treated wood contains toxic chemicals that can harm sheep.

quiz.q: How much manure does a 50-sheep flock produce per month?
quiz.explanation: A 50-sheep flock produces about 1 tonne of manure per month.

quiz.q: What is the recommended spacing for wooden posts in a permanent fence?
quiz.explanation: 3â4 metres provides good support for wire fencing.

quiz.q: What is a live fence?
options: B) A fence made of thorny plants like sisal or acacia
C) A wire fence with a dog
D) A fence that makes noise
quiz.explanation: Live fences use growing plants as a physical barrier.

quiz.q: How often should you check fences for breaks?
quiz.explanation: Weekly checks catch damage before sheep escape or predators enter.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a drafting gate?
options: A) To let sheep into the barn
B) To sort sheep into different groups
quiz.explanation: A drafting gate allows you to separate sheep by size, sex, or health status.

quiz.q: In cold highlands, what should you use on the windward side of a barn?
quiz.explanation: A solid wall blocks cold winds and protects sheep.

quiz.q: What is the recommended roof overhang to keep rain out?
quiz.explanation: A 50 cm overhang prevents rain from blowing into the barn.
